roster.name: Saquon Barkley
roster.outlook: Saquon Barkley did find the end zone last game for the Eagles, but was otherwise bottled up. Barkley managed just 22 yards on the ground along with the score in the 19-11 loss to the Giants before the bye. With third-string quarterback Joe Milton under center, Saquon will likely see a stacked box in Week 11 versus the Steelers. Pittsburgh has been stellar in defending the run in 2026 as well, allowing just 83.2 yards per tilt on the ground, which is third in the league. Likewise, Pittsburgh has yielded just five rushing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.

roster.name: Rashee Rice
roster.outlook: Rashee Rice's role and volume did not change much in Week 10 against the Falcons, even with trade deadline acquisition Josh Downs in the lineup for Kansas City. Rice caught five of six targets for 82 yards, the third time in seven games he's recorded at least 80 receiving yards. The fourth-year wide receiver is the top downfield option for Patrick Mahomes, but his 30-374-2 line on 38 targets is far from elite production. Rice will look to take a step forward in Week 11 against a Cardinals secondary that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Colston Loveland
roster.outlook: Colston Loveland will remain a top option in Chicago's passing game against the Saints in Week 11. Loveland has seen success lately after a shaky start to the season, surpassing 50 yards in his last four games and finding the end zone twice in that stretch. The second-year tight end has now posted a 37-363-2 receiving line off 57 targets in the first nine outings of the season. He'll face a New Orleans defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Jameson Williams
roster.outlook: Jameson Williams will remain a flashy option in Detroit's offense heading into Week 11 against the Buccaneers. Williams didn't benefit, like some of his teammates, from an offensive explosion in a Week 10 win over New England, but he still hauled in four of seven targets for 50 yards. The speedy wideout has now logged 32 catches for 518 yards and five touchdowns so far this season. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.

roster.name: Parker Washington
roster.outlook: Parker Washington capitalized on a favorable Week 10 matchup against the Titans, dissecting Tennessee's league-worst secondary for seven catches, a season-high 152 receiving yards, and a touchdown. Heading into a Week 11 road game against the Giants, Washington leads the Jaguars in all major receiving categories with a 36-645-6 line on 64 targets. He has had some down games with Trevor Lawrence spreading the ball around, as Washington has finished with a single catch on two occasions this season. That lower floor, compared to some of the elite wideouts around the NFL, makes Washington more of a fantasy WR2, but he offers weekly WR1 upside. The Giants are holding wideouts to 127 yards per game but have allowed 11 touchdown catches to the position in nine games.

roster.name: Emmett Johnson
roster.outlook: Emmett Johnson was incredible in his first career NFL start in Week 10 against the Falcons, leading Kansas City to a big win with 171 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The opportunity came with Kenneth Walker sidelined by a groin injury, but the issue isn't expected to keep the former Seahawk sidelined for long. Johnson's performance does make a case for him to take on a bigger workload as the No. 2 option in the backfield once Walker is back. Johnson will look to exploit what volume he gets in Week 11 against a Cardinals defense that's tied for 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Chase McLaughlin
roster.outlook: Chase McLaughlin could have limited scoring opportunities in the Buccaneers' Week 11 matchup against the Lions. McLaughlin has been one of fantasy's top kickers through nine games this season, converting on all 22 of his field-goal tries and all 18 of his point-after attempts. Despite this, he could have few scoring chances in Week 11 against a Detroit defense that's given up just 5.3 kicking points per game on the season.

roster.name: Bo Nix
roster.outlook: Bo Nix comes out of the Broncos' bye having built up a bit of momentum, producing multiple touchdowns in three straight games prior to the break while turning the ball over only once during that stretch. The third-year quarterback didn't get any reinforcements at the trade deadline, but the emergence of rookie Jonah Coleman in the backfield gives Denver a legitimate running option to help balance the offense, and second-year wideout Pat Bryant returned from IR right before the bye. In Week 11, Nix will take aim at a Raiders defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

roster.name: Kirk Cousins
roster.outlook: Kirk Cousins will take the reins again as the Vikings take on the 49ers in Week 11. Cousins shone in his Week 10 return to Minnesota, completing 68 percent of passes for 207 yards with a 2:1 TD:INT. The veteran will look to regain his form even more with his old squad this week ahead of what could be a tough matchup in Mexico City. The 49ers have ranked 14th in fantasy points allowed to QBs so far this season.

roster.name: James Cook III
roster.outlook: James Cook brings an eight-game scoring streak into the Bills' Week 11 matchup with the Dolphins. He has at least 18 carries in five straight games and has topped 100 rushing yards in five of nine outings overall. Cook hasn't caught a pass in two weeks, an area where Miami has been vulnerable, allowing five touchdown receptions to running backs, the same number of rushing touchdowns they've surrendered. A quick turnaround to a Week 12 Thursday night game is the only concern for Cook's workload and high-end production.

roster.name: Nico Collins
roster.outlook: Nico Collins has had an inconsistent season but remains a borderline fantasy WR1 for Houston's Week 11 matchup with a Colts defense that's allowing 149 yards per game to WRs and could be without top cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf). Collins drew 16 targets in the Week 10 loss to Cleveland after being targeted 14 times over the previous three games combined. His season average of 68 yards per game is his lowest mark since 2022. He exceeded 1,000 yards in every season from 2023 through 2025 but sits at just 478 yards through Houston's first nine games, two of which he missed due to a hamstring injury. Collins has scored five times in seven appearances and continues to work as the top target for C.J. Stroud.

roster.name: DeVonta Smith
roster.outlook: DeVonta Smith could return from a hamstring issue for the Eagles following their bye. Smith has missed five of the last six games for Philadelphia due to the ailment. His return, along with that of Dontayvion Wicks, would bolster an extremely depleted wide receiving corps. If he can suit up, the matchup could also be favorable in Week 11, as the Steelers defense has been surprisingly vulnerable to the pass in 2026. Pittsburgh is allowing 242.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

roster.name: D'Andre Swift
roster.outlook: D'Andre Swift will look to bounce back from a tough showing as the Bears play the Saints in Week 11. Swift was shelled by a tough Tampa Bay front before Chicago's Week 10 bye, rushing the ball 12 times for 31 yards. The veteran still racked up seven touchdowns in the preceding four games without Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) out, so there is still hope for him to deliver moving forward. Even if Monangai returns, New Orleans ranking 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs could allow for an entire backfield to eat.

roster.name: Rome Odunze
roster.outlook: Rome Odunze will aim to build on a season-best showing as the Bears play the Saints in Week 11. Odunze notched his first touchdown of the season and paired it with four catches for 60 yards in a Week 9 win over Tampa Bay before Chicago's bye week. The third-year pass catcher has now logged 32 receptions for 528 yards and a touchdown across nine games this season. He'll take on a New Orleans squad that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

roster.name: Justin Herbert
roster.outlook: Justin Herbert didn't need to do much with his arm in the Chargers' first win of the season, a Week 10 victory on Monday night over the Ravens. The quarterback threw for just 129 yards and failed to toss a touchdown for the third time in the last four games, but he did run in his first TD of the year. Herbert was missing top wide receiver Ladd McConkey once again, but the offense has been mostly ineffective even when McConkey has been healthy. Herbert will try to build on this performance in Week 11 against a Jets defense that ranks 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

roster.name: Travis Kelce
roster.outlook: Travis Kelce is coming off his least productive game of the season, catching both his targets for 30 yards in Kansas City's Week 10 win over the Falcons. The veteran tight end hasn't caught a touchdown pass since Week 3, and he hasn't hauled in more than five passes or 72 receiving yards since Week 2, but his role as Patrick Mahomes' most reliable security blanket gives him a fairly secure floor. Kelce will look to make a bigger contribution in Week 11 against a Cardinals defense that's tied for 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Eddy Pineiro
roster.outlook: Eddy Pineiro heads into a Week 11 clash versus Minnesota having been largely utilized for extra points thanks to San Francisco's highly efficient offense. Pineiro has gone just 8-for-11 on FG tries this season but leads the NFL with 35 PAT tries, of which he's made 31. That's largely because the 49ers have been extremely effective at getting into the end zone, and they are scoring 31.2 points per game -- second in the NFL. Something may have to give against the Vikings, who are allowing the fewest points per game (14.0) in the league.

roster.name: T.J. Hockenson
roster.outlook: T.J. Hockenson will aim to make a return as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. Hockenson missed his first game of the year in Week 10 against the Packers due to a wrist and chest injury. The veteran was unable to participate in practice prior to the matchup, so he'll likely need to get out there if he hopes to play in Mexico City. San Francisco has ranked middle-of-the-pack in fantasy points allowed to tight ends this season.

roster.name: Jonathan Taylor
roster.outlook: Jonathan Taylor exceeded 100 scrimmage yards for the fifth time in 10 tries during the Colts' Week 10 win over the Dolphins, but he was held without a touchdown for a third consecutive game. Seth McGowan has two rushing TDs during Taylor's three-game drought, both of which came from inside the 5-yard line. The rookie seventh-round pick could remain a thorn in Taylor's side if the Colts continue to give McGowan goal-line opportunities. McGowan's emergence, coupled with the Colts' offensive struggles as a team, knocks Taylor down to the fantasy RB1/RB2 borderline moving forward, and expectations should be tempered in Week 11 against a stout Texans front that limited Taylor to just 72 yards on 25 touches for a season-low 2.9 yards per touch in their first meeting this season. You're still starting Taylor if you have him in virtually every fantasy format, but he's likely to perform closer to his floor than his superstar ceiling in Week 11.

roster.name: Aaron Rodgers
roster.outlook: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers visit the Eagles for an interconference clash in Week 11. In Pittsburgh's Week 10 loss, he completed 15 of 29 pass attempts for 143 yards with two TDs and no INTs while rushing twice for minus-one yard. Rodgers and the entire Steelers offense struggled against the Bengals, which was not a very encouraging sign coming off a bye week. He'll try to bounce back versus a Philadelphia team allowing 21.4 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs.

roster.name: Malik Nabers
roster.outlook: Malik Nabers had a costly fumble last game for the Giants. Nabers had the ball punched out of his hands in scoring territory versus the Commanders, who ultimately defeated the G-Men by a score of 24-21. Nabers has now been held under 50 yards receiving in each of the last two outings following a dazzling four-game stretch of 100-yard outbursts. In Week 11, he will look to rebound against a Jacksonville defense that has been mediocre against the pass in 2026. The Jags are allowing 228.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 19th in the NFL.

roster.name: Cam Skattebo
roster.outlook: Cam Skattebo scored twice last game for the Giants. He also gained over 120 scrimmage yards for the second-straight contest. Following being benched versus the Saints, Skattebo has responded with 39 touches in the subsequent two tilts, though he did miss the win over Philadelphia due to a hamstring ailment. He will have his work cut out for him in Week 11 versus the Jags. Jacksonville is allowing just 91 rushing yards per clash, which is sixth in the NFL. In addition, the Jags have surrendered only five rushing touchdowns this season, which is tied for fourth in the league.

roster.name: Bucky Irving
roster.outlook: Bucky Irving will likely remain the focal points of the Buccaneers' offense during the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Irving has carried Tampa Bay's offense throughout the season, ranking sixth in the NFL in touches per game (21.0) and 10th in total yards per game (103.4). However, head coach Todd Bowles said that the Buccaneers "will try and lessen the load" on Irving following the team's Week 10 bye, suggesting he could see less work going forward. Additionally, Irving may struggle in Week 11 against a Lions defense that's held opposing running backs in check this season, allowing just 17.5 fantasy points per game.

roster.name: Trevor Lawrence
roster.outlook: Trevor Lawrence has thrown at least three touchdown passes in three of his last four starts and topped 300 passing yards in three of his last five, firmly placing him in the fantasy QB1 range for a Week 11 road game against the Giants. The 7-2 Jaguars and 5-3-1 Giants both lead their respective divisions, but Jacksonville's plus-125 point differential is far more impressive than the Giants' plus-7 mark. Pass defense has been a strength for the Giants, as they allow the third-fewest yards per game through the air (184). However, Lawrence maintains an elite ceiling regardless of opponent and could actually benefit statistically if this game remains close throughout, forcing the Jaguars to keep their foot on the gas. This season, he has thrown for 1,430 passing yards and 13 touchdowns in first halves, compared to 854 passing yards and eight touchdowns in second halves, with Jacksonville nursing large second-half leads on multiple occasions.

roster.name: Jordan Mason
roster.outlook: Jordan Mason will aim to make the most of his situation as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. Mason led Minnesota's backfield with 16 carries for 59 yards in a Week 10 win over the Packers, but teammate Aaron Jones punched in the only touchdown from the pair. Mason has yet to record a score in four outings since returning from a thumb injury, but he's put together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry. He'll face a San Francisco defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Braelon Allen
roster.outlook: Braelon Allen remains second fiddle to Breece Hall ahead of the Jets' Week 11 matchup with the Chargers. In two games since Hall's return, Allen has 16 carries compared to Hall's 26. Hall has also caught seven passes to Allen's three. Despite being more efficient than Hall, Allen's role appears clear in a matchup against a defense that's allowing a modest 4.0 yards per carry, likely rendering Allen to flex territory.

roster.name: Ollie Gordon II
roster.outlook: Ollie Gordon will have a heavy workload for as long as the Dolphins remain competitive in Week 11 against the Bills. Gordon has at least 16 carries in five straight games and caught a season-high four passes in Week 10, though Miami was in a four-quarter game against the Colts. Buffalo figures to be a far more difficult opponent, which could force a heavier pass-game script. With Buffalo allowing just 3.8 yards per carry, Gordon could be touchdown-dependent for top-end fantasy scoring.

roster.name: Jaylen Warren
roster.outlook: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to take on the Eagles in Week 11. He had seven carries for 15 yards and caught five of six targets for 26 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 10 loss. Warren and the entire Steelers offense found little success until the game was already out of reach, as several backups took the field in the fourth quarter. Warren will look to shake off the tough outing, but he'll have to do so against Philadelphia's seventh-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to opposing RBs.

roster.name: Chuba Hubbard
roster.outlook: Chubba Hubbard will continue operating as the Panthers' bell-cow back in the Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. Hubbard put Carolina on his back during the Week 10 win over the Saints, accumulating 172 yards and two touchdowns on 32 touches. On the season, Hubbard ranks fifth in the NFL in touches per game (21.3) eighth in scrimmage yards per game (106.4), suggesting he'll remain one of fantasy's top running backs as the year progresses. Despite this, he could struggle against a good Ravens defense that's allowed just 19.9 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs through nine games this season.

roster.name: Zay Flowers
roster.outlook: Zay Flowers and the Ravens look to snap a five-game losing streak when they visit the Panthers in Week 11. He corralled six of seven targets for 74 yards but lost a key fumble during Baltimore's Week 10 loss. Flowers turned it over with 2:11 remaining, ultimately ending his team's chance to tie or take the lead. On a brighter note, Jacoby Brissett attempted 49 passes and threw for 340 yards, meaning Flowers should have no shortage of opportunities to make up for the costly mistake versus Carolina's 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (31.5) to WRs.

roster.name: Spencer Shrader
roster.outlook: Spencer Shrader has made no more than one field goal in three of the last four games. His recent downturn has knocked Shrader out of first place in field goals made and attempted, though he's still top-three in both categories thanks to a torrid start that has the Colts' kicker at 23-for-25 through 10 games. That strong start included a 4-for-4 Week 3 performance against the Texans, whom Shrader will face again in Week 11. The Colts' offense has been depleted by a few trades and will likely struggle to generate consistent kicking opportunities moving forward, but Shrader is viable in Week 11 since Houston ranks in the middle of the pack with 24.3 points allowed per game and 18 made field goals against. If you see an enticing alternative on your league's waiver wire, it may be time to move on from Shrader.

roster.name: Dalton Kincaid
roster.outlook: A lack of opportunities could keep the Bills' Dalton Kincaid from exploiting the Dolphins' defense in Week 11. He had just three targets for the second straight game in Week 10, and his snap share has declined in each of the last three games since Buffalo's Week 7 bye, reaching a season-low 46% in Week 10. Buffalo has been a run-heavy offense, often leaving Kincaid off the field in favor of more traditional blocking tight ends. With declining snaps, he will be left with too few chances to beat a defense that's allowing the seventh-most fantasy points per game to the position.

roster.name: Brenton Strange
roster.outlook: Brenton Strange remains a borderline fantasy starter at TE for Week 11 against the Giants. He scored his first TD since Week 1 in Jacksonville's Week 10 win over the Titans but had just nine receiving yards, dropping his season average to 41 yards per game. That's right in line with the 48 receiving yards per game that the Giants allow to TEs, as they are a better-than-average defense against the position. Rookies Nate Boerkircher and Tanner Koziol have each recorded at least one catch in three consecutive games, but Strange remains the clear No. 1 TE for Jacksonville, handling a snap share north of 75%.

roster.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
roster.outlook: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep up his dominance as the Lions play the Buccaneers in Week 11. Gibbs had another monster performance in a Week 10 win over the Patriots, totaling 252 yards off 29 touches and tacking on two rushing touchdowns. The superstar has now amassed 1,384 scrimmage yards and 13 total touchdowns through nine showings. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to RBs.

roster.name: Ladd McConkey
roster.outlook: Ladd McConkey missed his third game of the season in Week 10, this time due to back trouble, as the Chargers' beat the Ravens for their first win of the season. McConkey's been fully healthy for only two games so far in 2026, posting an 8-152-0 line on 11 targets in those contests, and his only touchdown of the year came back in the first half of Week 1 before he suffered his initial rib injury, which was followed by a foot injury and a concussion. If McConkey is cleared to return in Week 11, he'll face a Jets secondary that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Joe Burrow
roster.outlook: Joe Burrow and the Bengals visit the Commanders on Monday Night Football in Week 11. His hot streak continued during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory, as he threw for 409 yards with four TDs and no INTs while rushing once for eight yards. Over his last five outings, all Bengals wins, Burrow has compiled 1,624 passing yards with a 20:3 TD:INT ratio, while adding 47 rushing yards and another two scores. The NFL's leading passer in terms of TDs (27) will aim to keep rolling versus the Commanders' 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (23.3) to opposing QBs.

roster.name: DK Metcalf
roster.outlook: In Week 11, DK Metcalf and the Steelers visit an Eagles defense allowing 37.9 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs. In Week 10, he hauled in two of six targets for 54 yards, including a 32-yard touchdown, during Pittsburgh's 38-18 loss. Metcalf found the end zone for just the second time all season and the first time since Week 3. Despite the favorable matchup, Metcalf remains an inconsistent fantasy option for a team that prefers to run the ball.

roster.name: Cameron Dicker
roster.outlook: Cameron Dicker booted three field goals for a third straight game, and the fifth time in the last seven, as the Chargers recorded their first win of 2026 in a Week 10 victory over the Ravens. The team's offensive struggles have created extra FG opportunities for its kicker, and Dicker has yet to kick more than two PATs in a game even as his field goal volume remains steady. That gives him a somewhat reliable floor, but a questionable ceiling, heading into a Week 11 clash with a Jets team allowing 25.4 points a contest, 22nd in the league.

roster.name: Brock Purdy
roster.outlook: Brock Purdy is coming off one of the best performances of his career as the 49ers prepare to host Minnesota in Week 11. Purdy threw for a career-best 389 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions this past Sunday in a win over Dallas. The star quarterback now ranks second among QBs with at least 100 pass attempts in QB rating (115.2) and has posted an impressive 20:5 TD:INT. However, Purdy faces a tough test in the Vikings, who lead the NFL with 37 sacks and have allowed only six passing touchdowns while recording 10 interceptions.

roster.name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
roster.outlook: Deebo Samuel will look to build on his best performance of the season when the 49ers  host the Vikings in Week 11. Samuel compiled 109 total yards and two touchdowns this past Sunday in a win over Dallas, with most of that yardage coming on a 70-yard rushing score. It was Samuel's first game if five weeks, as he had been sidelined due to a hamstring injury. His versatility could come in handy against a Vikings defense that is tied for the third-fewest receiving TDs (five) allowed to wideouts this season.

roster.name: Rico Dowdle
roster.outlook: In Week 11, Rico Dowdle and the Steelers visit the Eagles for an interconference tilt. He rushed five times for 26 yards and caught both targets for eight yards during Pittsburgh's 38-18 loss in Week 10. Dowdle and Jaylen Warren (7 carries, 15 yards) both struggled to make much of an impact, as the Steelers managed just 247 total yards of offense on the night. Dowdle could be more involved against an Eagles squad that has lost seven in a row, but Philadelphia's defense is allowing the seventh-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing RBs (19.7) in the league.

roster.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
roster.outlook: Amon-Ra St. Brown will seek to stay hot as the Lions play the Buccaneers in Week 11. St. Brown finally broke his touchdown drought in a Week 10 blowout win over New England, catching four of five targets for 98 yards and two scores. The star pass catcher has now posted a 65-755-7 receiving line on 91 targets across nine contests. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.

roster.name: Dallas Goedert
roster.outlook: Dallas Goedert collected five catches last game for Philadelphia, and continues to operate as a steady safety valve no matter who lines up under center. Goedert has at least four catches in all but one game played in 2026. In Week 11, Goedert will have a tasty matchup against a surprisingly porous Pittsburgh pass defense. The Steelers are surrendering 242.2 passing yards per clash, which is 30th in the NFL.

roster.name: Chig Okonkwo
roster.outlook: Chig Okonkwo has been a frequent target of quarterback Jayden Daniels since returning from injury for the Commanders. Okonkwo has at least six targets in four of the last five contests for Washington.  In fact, Okonkwo has been targeted 15 times over the last two games alone. Okonkwo is still looking for his first touchdown of the season, though. In Week 11, he will face a fairly stingy Cincinnati pass defense. The Bengals are allowing only 216.2 passing yards per clash, which is 11th in the league. Likewise, Cincy has given up just 11 throwing scores, which is tied for fifth in the NFL.

roster.name: Travis Etienne Jr.
roster.outlook: Travis Etienne will look to make a larger impact as the Saints' take on the Bears in Week 11. Etienne was relatively ineffective in his return from injury during the Week 10 loss to the Panthers, logging 11 touches for 34 yards. Despite Etienne serving as New Orleans' top running back, Audric Estime took most of the short-yardage work, and Alvin Kamara operated as the team's top red-zone back, scoring two touchdowns. Thus, Etienne's fantasy upside may be capped if his red-zone touches don't increase in the near future. He's set to face a solid Bears defense in Week 11 that's allowed just 20.4 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.

roster.name: Josh Allen
roster.outlook: Josh Allen faces potential workload limitations in the Bills' Week 11 game against the Dolphins. Allen completed only 11 of 21 passes against the Jets in Week 10, his second-lowest volume of the season, as Buffalo was able to get out to a comfortable lead and not challenge the Jets through the air. Another potentially uncompetitive game seems to be looming, and while Allen has 11 rushing touchdowns to go with his 13 passing scores, Miami has allowed quarterbacks to run for just two touchdowns all season. Allen routinely gets his fantasy points, but Week 11 expectations can be tempered slightly.

roster.name: Kenneth Walker III
roster.outlook: Kenneth Walker didn't suit up for Kansas City's Week 10 win over the Falcons due to a minor groin injury. In his place, rookie Emmett Johnson erupted for 171 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. Walker is expected back in Week 11 against Arizona, but Johnson's performance could lead to more volume for the team's backup RB as the focus shifts toward making sure Walker still has something left for the playoffs, given KC's 7-2 record. Assuming Walker is cleared to return, he'll be facing a Cardinals defense that's tied for 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Emeka Egbuka
roster.outlook: Emeka Egbuka is expected to lead the Buccaneers' receiving corps during the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Egbuka has had an underwhelming start to his 2026 season, catching 31 of 54 targets for 278 yards and two touchdowns in seven games. Despite this poor start, he ranks first on the Buccaneers in receiving yards, receptions, targets and touchdowns this year, suggesting more fantasy production is imminent. Egbuka could thrive against the Lions' secondary in Week 11, as they have allowed 32.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wide receiver groups this season.

roster.name: DJ Moore
roster.outlook: DJ Moore will seek more big plays in Week 11 when the Bills face the Dolphins. Moore is averaging 16.3 yards per catch, the second-highest mark of his nine-year career, and gets an inviting matchup with a secondary that's allowing 9.3 yards per target to wideouts, the sixth-highest mark league-wide. Moore will need those big yardage chances as Buffalo threw only 21 times in Week 10 while blowing out the Jets, and a similar game script is likely against Miami.

roster.name: Luther Burden III
roster.outlook: Luther Burden will aim to recover from a concussion ahead of Chicago's Week 11 game against the Saints. Burden got concussed in the fourth quarter of a Week 9 win over the Buccaneers before the Bears' bye week, so hopefully he's had enough time to heal. The second-year star has now posted a 49-644-4 receiving line across nine games with career highs in catches and touchdowns, with one more game likely to get him over the hump in yards as well. If he's active, Burden will face a New Orleans defense that's ranked a tough eighth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Courtland Sutton
roster.outlook: Courtland Sutton caught a season-high five passes in the Broncos' last game before their Week 10 bye, turning one of the receptions into his second touchdown of the season. The veteran wide receiver's target volume increased after Jaylen Waddle left the contest early due to a concussion. He has yet to reach 50 receiving yards or see double-digit targets in any game this year as the No. 2 option in a sluggish passing game. Sutton will attempt to contribute in Week 11 against a Raiders secondary that ranks 24th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Kyle Monangai
roster.outlook: Kyle Monangai will look to make a return as the Bears play the Saints in Week 11. Monangai has sat out five straight games as he works back from a turf-toe injury. The second-year ball carrier's status is very likely correlated with his ability to practice, so this week should reveal his expected return timeline. He accrued 324 rushing yards and three touchdowns off 60 carries in the first four games of the season. If he returns, Monangai will face a New Orleans defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs this season.

roster.name: Alvin Kamara
roster.outlook: Alvin Kamara will remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Kamara was limited to just five touches while Travis Etienne returned from injury in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers. However, Kamara scored two touchdowns on those touches and appeared to be operating as New Orleans' top red-zone RB. With Kamara, Etienne and Audric Estime all playing roles in the Saints' backfield, it may be hard to trust any of them going forward. Kamara could take advantage of a Chicago defense that's allowed 7.3 yards per target and two receiving touchdowns to opposing RBs this season.

roster.name: Tre Tucker
roster.outlook: Tre Tucker didn't show much chemistry with Fernando Mendoza in the rookie quarterback's first NFL start, catching just one of two targets for nine yards in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. He remains the team's top wide receiver, and with Brock Bowers now dealing with an ankle injury, there could be less competition for targets in the short term. Tucker produced a 34-538-4 line on 58 targets through the first nine games of the year, mainly with Kirk Cousins under center. He'll try to establish that kind of rapport with Mendoza in Week 11 against a Broncos secondary that ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Tyler Bass
roster.outlook: Tyler Bass faces unsettled scoring chances when the Bills host the Dolphins in Week 11. After attempting multiple field goals in five straight games, Bass tried just one in Week 10 with Buffalo coasting to a win and converting drives into touchdowns. That script seems likely to manifest again in Week 11 against an overmatched Miami defense, so while Bass will have a multi-PAT floor, his ceiling could be capped.

roster.name: Darren Waller
roster.outlook: Darren Waller is expected to remain the Panthers' top receiving option at tight end during the Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. Despite Waller leading Carolina's tight end corps in receptions (25), targets (38) and receiving yards (323) through nine games this year, he's been super inconsistent as of late. The veteran has logged two-or-fewer receptions in four of his last five games, with the exception coming in the Week 9 loss to the Broncos, in which he caught eight of 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown. Waller is likely too inconsistent to start right now, despite a strong Week 11 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed six touchdowns to opposing TEs through nine contests this season.

roster.name: Ja'Marr Chase
roster.outlook: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals face the Commanders in an interconference clash on Monday Night Football in Week 11. He corralled 11 of 14 targets for a season-high 231 yards during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory. After failing to eclipse the 100-yard mark through his first six outings, Chase has done so in three consecutive contests, gaining more than 140 receiving yards in each. He'll take a 64-878-7 line on 87 targets into a matchup against Washington's 20th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (33.5) to WRs.

roster.name: Breece Hall
roster.outlook: Breece Hall brings steady volume into a somewhat challenging matchup in Week 11 when the Jets face the Chargers. Hall has amassed at least 11 carries in both games since returning from injury while adding seven receptions, tallying 195 total yards though not reaching the end zone and continuing to share reps with Braelon Allen. The Chargers are allowing the 10th most fantasy points per game to opposing backs, but just 4.0 yards per carry and an even lower 3.9 yards per reception. Hall remains a lineup mainstay and could surge in the receiving game if Cade Klubnik is forced into action over Geno Smith (ankle).

roster.name: David Montgomery
roster.outlook: David Montgomery (groin) remained sidelined for Houston's Week 10 loss against the Browns despite practicing without limitations the Friday preceding the game. He hasn't played since Week 5, but Montgomery has the green light to suit up against the Colts in Week 11 and is in line for a prominent role, as Woody Marks (concussion) will miss Thursday's game on a short week after getting hurt in Week 10. No other RB besides Montgomery or Marks has more than 13 carries for the Texans this season. Despite averaging just 2.7 yards per carry prior to his injury, Montgomery has RB2 upside given the lack of competition for backfield opportunities against a Colts defense that's allowing 151 scrimmage yards and a touchdown per game to RBs.

roster.name: Carnell Tate
roster.outlook: Carnell Tate hasn't played since Week 7 due to a shoulder injury. Prior to his absence, the rookie fourth overall pick had at least 69 receiving yards in three of his last four appearances. If Tate gets the green light to play in Week 11, he would be a high-end flex option against a Dallas defense that's allowing 158 yards and a TD per game through the air to wide receivers. Titans QB Cam Ward is coming off his two best outings of the season in Tate's absence.

roster.name: Sam LaPorta
roster.outlook: Sam LaPorta will aim to get back on track as the Lions return home against the Patriots in Week 11. LaPorta has had an extremely dry stretch ever since Detroit's bye week, failing to reach 40 yards in four straight games. The starting tight end has now recorded 36 receptions for 415 yards and three touchdowns, with most of his volume coming from the first five outings of the season. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Woody Marks
roster.outlook: Woody Marks entered concussion protocol during Houston's Week 10 loss to the the Browns. He isn't expected to be cleared in time to face the Colts on Thursday Night Football in Week 11. David Montgomery (groin) would likely assume the lead role in Houston's backfield if he gains clearance for his first action since Week 5. Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale are Houston's other options at RB.

roster.name: Jared Goff
roster.outlook: Jared Goff will aim to take some momentum into Week 11 as the Lions play the Buccaneers. Goff broke a two-game stretch of struggles in a Week 10 win over the Patriots, completing 65 percent of passes for 303 yards with a 3:2 TD:INT. The veteran has now dished out 18 touchdowns with 2,437 passing yards across nine games this campaign. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked top five in fantasy points allowed to QBs.

roster.name: Cam Little
roster.outlook: Cam Little has gone 4-for-4 on field-goal attempts in each of Jacksonville's last two games, with that two-game stretch accounting for nearly half of his 18 made field goals this season. The Jaguars are consistently moving the ball into scoring range, and while they have been adept at scoring TDs rather than settling for FGs, the team's offensive prowess coupled with Little's big leg keeps Jacksonville's kicker safely in the set-and-forget starter range. In Week 11, Little will face the Giants on the road. MetLife Stadium is one of the tougher kicking environments in the NFL, and the Giants' opponents have made just nine field goals in nine games, but the surging Little has the potential to make fantasy managers who over-index on the matchup look silly given his high ceiling.

roster.name: Jordyn Tyson
roster.outlook: Jordyn Tyson will look to build on his breakout performance in the Saints' Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Tyson was one of New Orleans' few bright spots in the Week 11 loss to the Panthers, catching 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in his second NFL game. He's clearly established himself as one of the Saints' top two receiving options but could struggle if Chris Olave is more involved in Week 11. Tyson could thrive against a solid Bears secondary, however, as they have allowed 9.2 yards per target to opposing WRs this year.

roster.name: CeeDee Lamb
roster.outlook: CeeDee Lamb continues to pile up statistics for the Dallas Cowboys. Lamb found the end zone for the second-straight game and eighth time overall in 2026 in the 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Lamb finished with seven catches for 72 yards and the score. Lamb has drawn double-digit targets in five-straight contests, a trend that should continue in Week 11 versus the Titans. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.

roster.name: Justin Jefferson
roster.outlook: Justin Jefferson could be in store for better output again as the Vikings play San Francisco in Week 11. Jefferson benefited from the addition of Kirk Cousins to Minnesota in a Week 10 win over Green Bay, logging season highs in catches (9) and targets (13). The star wideout's 74 yards were also his best total since Week 5, further supporting that he may be in store for a return to dominance. He'll take on a 49ers defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this campaign.

roster.name: Garrett Wilson
roster.outlook: Garrett Wilson continues to dominate targets in the Jets' passing game ahead of a Week 11 matchup with the Chargers. He garnered a season-high 14 targets in Week 10, his fourth outing with double-digit looks, while topping 100 yards for the third time. Wilson has only three touchdowns on the year and faces a bit of quarterback uncertainty with Geno Smith dealing with an ankle injury, but the Chargers have allowed 11 receivers to score in nine games and have surrendered 340-plus passing yards in consecutive weeks. With steady volume, Wilson profiles as a safe lineup cog in Week 11.

roster.name: Javonte Williams
roster.outlook: Javonte Williams was held out of the end zone for the second time in three games for the Cowboys. Williams rushed 16 times for 63 yards in the 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Williams was also held under 65 yards rushing for the second time in three contests. However, his usage remains high, as he has received double-digit carries in every game in 2026. In Week 11, Williams will face a Titans squad that has been lackluster against the run. Tennessee is allowing 124 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 22nd in the league.

roster.name: Bhayshul Tuten
roster.outlook: Bhayshul Tuten has scored six times during his current four-game TD streak, and he has mustered at least 87 scrimmage yards in seven of Jacksonville's nine games this season. The second-year stud has crept into fantasy RB1 territory ahead of Jacksonville's Week 11 road game against the Giants, who have allowed just four rushing TDs to RBs but also three receiving TDs to the position through nine games. Tuten has five rushing TDs and three receiving scores this season while notching at least 12 carries in every game and two-plus receptions in all but two outings. His well-rounded skill set allows Jacksonville's lead back to maintain a prominent role regardless of the score.

roster.name: Tyler Warren
roster.outlook: Tyler Warren had a season-low three targets in a head-scratching Week 10 performance against the Dolphins after the Colts traded away starting WRs Josh Downs and Keenan Allen. Even after that dud, Warren is still averaging a healthy seven targets per game, and his 276 receiving yards and two receiving TDs lead all players still rostered by the Colts. Warren had a season-high nine catches when the Colts faced the Texans in Week 3 and should be similarly busy in the Week 11 rematch against a Houston defense that ranks among the league's 10 most generous units through the air. Don't let Warren's down game in Week 10 dissuade you from continuing to deploy him as a high-floor fantasy starter at TE.

roster.name: Dak Prescott
roster.outlook: Dak Prescott tied a career high with five touchdown passes last game for Dallas. Unfortunately, the Cowboys defense could not stop a nosebleed, as they fell by a staggering score of 46-40 to the 49ers. Dak also threw for a season-high 343 yards, notching his second-straight 300-yard output overall. Dak has tossed multiple touchdowns in three of the last four contests. In Week 11, Dak will look to keep rolling against a suspect Tennessee pass defense. The Titans are allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.

roster.name: Mike Evans
roster.outlook: Mike Evans reportedly has a chance to return from an Achilles injury for San Francisco's Week 11 tilt against the Vikings. Evans has missed the 49ers' past three games while dealing with right Achilles tendinitis. San Francisco recently acquired veteran Keenan Allen to bolster the wideout corps, and Deebo Samuel returned in Week 10 from a multi-game absence caused by a hamstring injury, but Evans' ability to get back on the field would still be a big boost given his chemistry with QB Brock Purdy this season. The 49ers can use all the help they can get on Sunday Night Football, as Minnesota has been tough on opposing passing games this season and has allowed just 16.2 fantasy points per game to wideouts -- fourth-best in the NFL.

roster.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
roster.outlook: Chris Godwin is expected to operate as Tampa Bay's No. 2 wideout during the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Coming off a Week 10 bye, Godwin ranks second on the Buccaneers in receiving yards (259), receptions (29) and targets (39). Despite being one of Tampa's top pass catchers, his fantasy production has been limited by the team's lack of a passing attack, which could continue in Week 11 as Baker Mayfield (foot/ankle) deals with an injury. However, Godwin could find success against a Detroit defense that's allowed 7.7 yards per target to opposing wideouts this year.

roster.name: Jordan Addison
roster.outlook: Jordan Addison is set to remain out as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. Addison missed a Week 10 win over Green Bay with a thumb injury, and he's likely to require a possible IR-designating surgery. Jauan Jennings (calf), Myles Price and Tai Felton could all see an uptick in usage with Addison inactive.

roster.name: Mark Andrews
roster.outlook: In Week 11, Mark Andrews and the Ravens look to snap a five-game losing streak when they visit the 4-5 Panthers. He's coming off easily his best outing of the season in Week 10's loss, as he caught all eight of his targets for 82 yards while leading the team in receptions and yardage. Andrews established new season highs in each receiving category with the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett making his first start for Baltimore. Brissett attempted 49 passes and threw for 340 yards, and if that trend continues for the Ravens' offense, Andrews could be primed for a much larger role moving forward.

roster.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
roster.outlook: Ka'imi Fairbairn is 19-for-20 on field-goal attempts and 24-for-24 on PAT tries for the Texans heading into a Week 11 home game against the Colts. Indianapolis is tied for the second-most made field goals allowed (21) and is surrendering 27.1 points per game overall. Fairbairn is a set-and-forget fantasy starter at the kicker position, as usual, in Week 11 as the 3-6 Texans try to bolster their dwindling playoff hopes.

roster.name: Jakobi Meyers
roster.outlook: Jakobi Meyers ranks second on the Jaguars behind Parker Washington in both receiving yards (408) and targets (43), but the gap between Washington and Meyers is far larger than the gap between Meyers and TE Brenton Strange for the role of Trevor Lawrence's No. 2 target. Meyers has exceeded 65 yards just once all season and hasn't scored since Week 3, so he has been a disappointment more often than not for fantasy managers plugging him into a flex spot. He'll have a decent opportunity to end his six-game touchdown drought in Week 11 against a Giants secondary that has allowed WRs to score 11 times in nine games, though the Giants hold wideouts to just 127 yards per game. As usual, Meyers is a fine deep-league flex but not a player to get particularly excited about.

roster.name: Ashton Jeanty
roster.outlook: Ashton Jeanty failed to generate much production in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, gaining 18 rushing yards on nine carries and catching all four of his targets for 46 yards. It's the sixth time in the last seven games he's generated more yards through the air than on the ground, but his hold on the No. 1 job in the backfield may have tightened a bit with Mike Washington struggling over the last two weeks as well. Jeanty's outlook as a pass-catcher could improve if Brock Bowers misses time due to an ankle injury. During the two games the star tight end sat out at the beginning of the season, Jeanty caught 10 of 13 targets for 60 yards and two touchdowns. He'll try to break out in Week 11 against a Broncos defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Trey McBride
roster.outlook: Trey McBride is set to work with rookie quarterback Carson Beck for the second time when the Cardinals travel to Kansas City for a Week 11 clash. McBride had his season-opening streak of logging at least seven receptions snapped this past Sunday in a loss to the Rams, when he managed a quiet 5-37-0 receiving line on five targets. Nonetheless, every part of his line (catches, receiving yardage and targets) led the Cardinals in a game during which Beck struggled mightily to move the ball. There could be an opportunity for McBride to post better numbers against Kansas City, who have given up the fifth-most fantasy points per game (9.8) to tight ends this season.

roster.name: Tetairoa McMillan
roster.outlook: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain Carolina's top wideout during the Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. McMillan was limited to just three catches on seven targets during the Week 10 win over the Saints, his fewest reception total since the Week 3 loss to the Browns. However, he ranked first on the team in targets while the rest of Carolina's receiver room combined for five targets, which is positive sign for McMillan's fantasy outlook going forward. McMillan could thrive against the Ravens in Week 11, as they have given up 34.3 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through nine games this season.

roster.name: Tee Higgins
roster.outlook: Tee Higgins and the Bengals visit Washington on Monday Night Football in Week 11. He brought in five of six targets for 66 yards during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory, extending the team's win streak to five games. Higgins' consecutive outings with a TD snapped, however, as he failed to find the end zone for the first time since Week 5. Head coach Zac Taylor relayed Higgins' workload was being managed toward the end of the win over Pittsburgh, so keep an eye on his status in practice during Week 11 prep.

roster.name: Tony Pollard
roster.outlook: Tony Pollard has racked up 391 scrimmage yards and six touchdowns over Tennessee's last three games, putting him in the fantasy RB1 conversation for a Week 11 trip to Dallas. After a pair of dominant rushing performances, Pollard struggled to find running room against Jacksonville's elite front in Week 10 but racked up 66 receiving yards and a TD on a career-high eight catches. The former Cowboys RB is locked into a workhorse role for the Titans, and Pollard's old team has given up the most fantasy production in the league to RBs, allowing 155 scrimmage yards per game, as well as a league-high 16 total TDs to the position through 10 games.

roster.name: Brandon Aubrey
roster.outlook: Brandon Aubrey connected on two field goals and two extra points for the Cowboys in the 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Aubrey did miss an extra point, his second of the season. However, both of Aubrey's field goals came from 50-plus yards out, giving him five such field goals on the season to date. In Week 11, Dallas will face a bumbling Titans squad. Tennessee is allowing 26.6 points per contest, which is 27th in the league.

roster.name: Aaron Jones Sr.
roster.outlook: Aaron Jones will look to build off a solid showing as the Vikings travel to San Francisco in Week 11. Jones did well against his former squad in Week 10, logging 47 rushing yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, along with catching one pass for eight yards. The veteran remains in a timeshare with Jordan Mason, but he still holds some value moving forward. The 49ers have ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs this campaign.

roster.name: Khalil Shakir
roster.outlook: Khalil Shakir is in search of a bounce-back outing in Week 11 when the Bills face the Dolphins. He logged only three targets in Week 10, the second time this season he's had such low volume, and now has four games with 38 yards or fewer in nine outings. Buffalo threw only 21 times against the Jets, and if they jump to a big lead again against Miami, a similar game flow could emerge, potentially giving Shakir too few opportunities to better a secondary that's allowing 9.3 yards per target.

roster.name: Isaiah Likely
roster.outlook: Isaiah Likely notched a career-high 127 yards receiving last game for the Giants. Likely reeled in nine passes, one of which went for a 66-yard touchdown, though the G-Men fell to Washington by a score of 24-21. Still, Likely has scored in back-to-back contests, and has five scores in his last five outings.  In Week 11, the Giants will face a Jacksonville defense that has been mediocre against the pass in 2026. The Jags are allowing 228.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 19th in the NFL. However, Jacksonville has surrendered just 10 passing scores this season, which is fourth in the NFL.

roster.name: Xavier Worthy
roster.outlook: Xavier Worthy could be in danger of vanishing from the Kansas City game plan. In a Week 10 win over the Falcons that marked the debut of trade-deadline acquisition Josh Downs, Worthy registered only three targets and failed to catch any. Downs, meanwhile, caught four of five targets and got into the end zone despite playing just 10 snaps. As the former Colt's role increases, Worthy could be squeezed further for looks from Patrick Mahomes, with Rashee Rice, Travis Kelce, and the team's running backs also seemingly ahead of him in the pecking order. Worthy will try to bounce back in Week 11 against a Cardinals secondary that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Bryce Young
roster.outlook: Bryce Young is expected to continue leading the Panthers' offense during the Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. Young had a relatively underwhelming performance in the Week 10 win over the Saints, completing 17 of 30 passes for 200 yards without a touchdown or interception. Despite this outing, Young ranks sixth in the NFL in pass attempts (37.6) and yards (266.3) per game, suggesting a positive fantasy outlook moving forward. However, Young could struggle against a solid Ravens defense that's given up just 20.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks through nine games this year.

roster.name: Cam Ward
roster.outlook: Cam Ward has taken a noticeable step forward in Tennessee's last two games, even though the Titans lost both to drop to 1-8. After throwing for a career-high 304 yards and tossing multiple touchdown passes for the first time this season against the Bengals, Ward threw for 231 yards and two TDs in the Week 10 loss to Jacksonville, his second-highest passing yards total of the campaign. His four touchdown passes in that two-game stretch match Ward's total from his first seven starts of the season. The improving 2025 first overall pick has a nice opportunity to keep building momentum in Week 11 against a dreadful Dallas defense that has surrendered a 19:4 TD:INT ratio en route to allowing 28.2 points per game. Ward's underwhelming larger body of work leaves him out of the starting mix in most single-QB formats, but he's a sneaky-good Week 11 superflex option.
