roster.name: Derrick Henry
roster.outlook: Derrick Henry and the Ravens take to the road in Week 11 to battle the 4-5 Panthers. In Baltimore's Week 10 loss, he rushed 10 times for 10 yards and two touchdowns and caught all five of his targets for 10 yards. Henry was able to salvage an otherwise miserable outing with two scores, the 32-year-old's ninth and tenth rushing TDs on the season. The Ravens attempted 49 passes with Jacoby Brissett making his team debut under center. The hope is that Brissett will allow Henry more breathing room between the tackles versus Carolina's 29th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (27.3) to opposing RBs.

roster.name: Brock Bowers
roster.outlook: Brock Bowers played just 11 offensive snaps in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks due to an ankle injury, catching both his targets for 18 yards. The star tight end's injury isn't thought to be too serious, but he could miss at least a game or two, potentially opening the door for Michael Mayer to have a bigger role. If Bowers is able to suit up in Week 11 and continue building chemistry with rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, he'll be taking on a Broncos defense that ranks 30th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Patrick Mahomes
roster.outlook: Patrick Mahomes is coming off a huge performance in a Week 10 win over the Falcons, as he threw five touchdown passes for the first time since Week 1 of the 2022 season. The trade-deadline addition of Josh Downs revitalized the passing game, as four different Kansas City players had receptions of 30-plus yards. Mahomes has a 10:0 TD:INT ratio over the last three games with two 300-yard performances, giving him significant momentum heading into a Week 11 clash with a Cardinals defense that ranks 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

roster.name: Harrison Butker
roster.outlook: Harrison Butker hasn't converted a field goal attempt in two straight games and hasn't kicked more than one in four straight, going a weak 2-for-6 on attempts during that stretch. The Kansas City offense has been providing him with more PATs, however, and he's gone 13-for-13 on extra points over the last three contests. Butker's struggles have left him with little job security, but for now he still holds the job. He could be busier in Week 11 against a Cardinals team allowing 28.9 points per game, tied for 31st in the league with the Raiders.

roster.name: Michael Mayer
roster.outlook: Michael Mayer could be set for a significant role in the Raiders' passing game in the short term. In a Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, Brock Bowers suffered an ankle injury, and while it's not thought to be serious, he could be sidelined for a game or two. Mayer caught two of three targets for 16 yards against Seattle, but his volume from rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza would likely increase with Bowers off the field. If Mayer's volume does increase in Week 11, it will come against a Broncos defense that ranks 30th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Keenan Allen
roster.outlook: Keenan Allen is coming off an impactful 49ers debut heading into a Week 11 matchup versus Minnesota. After being acquired by San Francisco at the trade deadline, Allen caught five of seven targets for 61 yards this past Sunday in a win over Dallas. Despite having a relatively short amount of time to learn his new team's offense, Allen looked to have good chemistry with QB Brock Purdy, which is an encouraging sign for his production moving forward. His work as a possession receiver could be especially useful against the Vikings, who own the highest blitz rate in the NFL.

roster.name: Devaughn Vele
roster.outlook: Devaughn Vele is expected to operate as the Saints' No. 3 wideout during the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Since 2026 first-round pick Jordyn Tyson returned from injury in the Week 9 win over the Browns, Vele has caught just four of six targets for 31 yards. It appears as if his role on New Orleans' offense has diminished, suggesting his fantasy value is limited without scoring a touchdown on a weekly basis. He's set to face a solid Chicago secondary in Week 11 that's given up just eight receiving touchdowns to wideouts through nine games this season.

roster.name: Chase Brown
roster.outlook: In Week 11, Chase Brown and the Bengals travel to face the Commanders on Monday Night Football. In Week 10, during Cincinnati's victory, he rushed 10 times for 44 yards and caught eight of nine targets for 39 yards and two TDs. Brown finally found paydirt, doing so for the first time since Week 1, while recording his first two receiving scores of the season. He'll look to exploit a Commanders defense that gave up 78 yards and two TDs to Cam Skattebo in their previous outing.

roster.name: George Pickens
roster.outlook: George Pickens snagged three touchdowns last game for the Cowboys. Pickens racked up an incredible 18 targets, parlaying those looks into 11 grabs for 145 yards and the three scores. The targets and receptions set career highs, while the yardage total was his best on the season. In Week 11, Pickens has a delectable matchup against the Titans. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.

roster.name: Germie Bernard
roster.outlook: Germie Bernard and the Steelers are in Philadelphia for a Week 11 interconference clash. He failed to bring in any of his three targets during Week 10's loss to Cincinnati but did gain 10 yards on his lone carry. Bernard was held without a catch for the first time since Week 1, when he played only three offensive snaps. Pittsburgh's offense struggled all night, gaining just 247 total yards, but the hope is that Bernard will bounce back versus an Eagles defense allowing 37.9 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs.

roster.name: C.J. Stroud
roster.outlook: C.J. Stroud tossed three more touchdown passes in Houston's Week 10 loss to the Browns, bringing his TD:INT ratio to 19:3 through nine games, with 13 of those scores coming in his last four outings. The fourth-year QB's brilliance has largely been wasted on the 3-6 Texans, as the defense and running game have both declined from last season. Houston's playoff hopes aren't extinguished yet, but Stroud can't afford a Week 11 letdown in a home rematch against a Colts defense that held him to 167 yards and one TD in Week 3, when the Texans lost 19-17 at Indianapolis. The 3-7 Colts have allowed a 16:2 TD:INT ratio, so Stroud is worth starting in this Week 11 rematch Thursday despite his poor performance in the first meeting between these AFC South rivals.

roster.name: Stefon Diggs
roster.outlook: Stefon Diggs has scored in three of his last four games played for Washington. Diggs scored the game-winning touchdown last Thursday versus the Giants to bring his season total for receiving touchdowns to six. Diggs also posted a season-high 83 receiving yards for the game. He was targeted 10 times for the game, and should continue to see increased looks in the absence if Terry McLaurin. However, in Week 11, he will be facing a Bengals defense allowing just 216.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. In addition, Cincy has yielded just 11 passing scores, which is tied for fifth in the NFL.

roster.name: Jonah Coleman
roster.outlook: Jonah Coleman captured the No. 1 job in the Broncos' backfield prior to the team's bye. Over the team's last two games, the rookie running back amassed 192 scrimmage yards and two rushing TDs, with his yardage split almost equally between the ground and the air. Coleman's usage as a pass catcher could decline once RJ Harvey gets healthy in a couple of weeks, but he's clearly surpassed J.K. Dobbins as the preferred ball carrier in all situations, including at the goal line. Coleman will take on a Raiders defense in Week 11 that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Devin Singletary
roster.outlook: Devin Singletary played just five snaps last game for the Giants. With Cam Skattebo healthy, Singletary was left largely riding the pine, a spot he will likely continue to occupy in Week 11 versus the Jags. The matchup versus Jacksonville is also far from ideal. Jacksonville is allowing just 91 rushing yards per clash, which is sixth in the NFL. In addition, the Jags have surrendered only five rushing touchdowns this season, which is tied for fourth in the league.

roster.name: Christian McCaffrey
roster.outlook: Christian McCaffrey enters San Francisco's Week 11 matchup against Minnesota on the heels of one of the biggest performances of his career. In this past Sunday's win over Dallas, McCaffrey recorded a career-best 161 receiving yards en route to 223 total yards and three touchdowns. The star RB has logged at least one TD in each of his past eight games and has multiple scores in three of his past four contests, making him an elite week-to-week fantasy asset. With that said, McCaffrey is slated for a tough matchup against the Vikings, who rank eighth in the NFL by allowing 15.3 fantasy points per game to running backs.

roster.name: Omarion Hampton
roster.outlook: Omarion Hampton is coming off his best performance of the season in the Chargers' Week 10 win over the Ravens, topping 100 rushing yards for the first time and scoring his first touchdown since Week 4. It was a big step toward Hampton regaining the clear No. 1 job in the backfield, as Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal combined for just seven touches and 18 scrimmage yards. Hampton will look to keep rolling in Week 11 against a Jets defense that's tied for 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Chris Olave
roster.outlook: Chris Olave is expected to bounce back from an underwhelming performance in the Saints' Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Olave was overshadowed by 2026 first-round pick Jordyn Tyson in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers, as he logged season-lows in targets, receptions and yards. Despite this poor showing, Olave remains eighth in the NFL in receiving yards per game (84.9) and 10th in targets per game (9.7), so his fantasy outlook remains very positive going forward. However, he's set to face a tough Bears defense that's allowed just 29.4 fantasy points per game to opposing wide receivers this season.

roster.name: Jaylen Waddle
roster.outlook: Jaylen Waddle sustained a concussion in the Broncos' final game before their bye, winding up with just a 22-yard reception on his only target. The former Dolphin has struggled to adjust to his new offense, and through nine games this season he's produced a 30-337-2 line on 52 targets, putting him on pace for a career low in receiving yards. Assuming he clears the concussion protocol in time to suit up in Week 11, he'll be facing a Raiders secondary that ranks 24th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Jayden Daniels
roster.outlook: Jayden Daniels tossed three touchdown passes last game for the Commanders. He also threw his first two interceptions of the season in the thrilling 24-21 win over the Giants. Daniels has thrown for at least 215 yards in four-straight contests. He may be more successful with his legs than with his arm in Week 11 versus the Bengals, though. Cincinnati is allowing just 216.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the NFL. By contrast, Cincy is surrendering 123.9 rushing yards per clash, which is 21st in the league.

roster.name: George Kittle
roster.outlook: George Kittle continues to be one of the NFL's most consistent tight ends ahead of the 49ers' Week 11 clash with Minnesota. Kittle tallied six catches for 74 yards this past Sunday in a win over Dallas, marking his eighth straight contest with at least four receptions. He's also registered at least 58 yards seven times during that span, giving him a very reliable weekly floor. Kittle could find the sledding tough against Minnesota, though, as the Vikings have given up the fewest fantasy points per game (5.1) to wideouts this season.

roster.name: Josh Downs
roster.outlook: Josh Downs made an immediate difference in his Kansas City debut, catching four of five targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's win over the Falcons despite running just eight routes and playing only 10 snaps. Picked up from the Colts at the trade deadline, Downs' efficiency on a limited workload bodes well, but he'll still be the No. 2 wide receiver behind Rashee Rice, with Travis Kelce and the team's running backs also factoring significantly into the passing game. Downs will try to build on this performance in Week 11 against a Cardinals secondary that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Jake Bates
roster.outlook: Jake Bates will look to stay reliable as the Lions play the Buccaneers in Week 11. Bates didn't attempt a field goal in a Week 10 win over the Patriots, but 5 XPAs kept his performance solid. The starting boot has now converted 16 of 17 field-goal attempts and made all 29 of his extra-point tries across nine games this campaign. He'll face a Tampa defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy kickers.

roster.name: Dominic Zvada
roster.outlook: Dominic Zvada somehow still has a job following yet another missed field goal for the Giants. Zvada missed a 33-yarder in the 24-21 loss to the Commanders. He has missed six field goals to date, including three from under 50 yards out. In Week 11, points will likely be difficult to come by versus the Jags. Jacksonville is allowing just 16 points per tilt, which is second in the NFL.

roster.name: Samaje Perine
roster.outlook: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to take on the Commanders in Week 11. He rushed six times for 14 yards and a touchdown and caught all four targets for 25 yards during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory. Perine watched as Chase Brown produced 83 yards and two TDs on 18 touches, with both backs helping the Bengals win a fifth straight game. Perine has been valuable to Cincinnati's offense, but his limited role doesn't offer fantasy upside with Brown still atop the depth chart.

roster.name: Antonio Williams
roster.outlook: Antonio Williams found the end zone last game for Washington. The rookie snagged two passes for 42 yards and a touchdown in the 24-21 win over the G-Men. Williams has at least two catches in every game this season, and should continue to see steady work in the absence of Terry McLaurin. However, in Week 11, he will be facing a Bengals defense allowing just 216.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. In addition, Cincy has yielded just 11 passing scores, which is tied for fifth in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Will Reichard
free_agents.outlook: Will Reichard will seek to stay hot as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. Reichard was perfect in a Week 10 win over Green Bay, nailing all six of his kicks with three field-goal makes. The third-year kicker has now converted 23 of 25 field-goal attempts and made all 13 of his XPAs across nine showings. The 49ers have allowed a middle-of-the-pack 8.0 points per game to kickers this season.

free_agents.name: Jalen Coker
free_agents.outlook: Jalen Coker will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Panthers' Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. After catching 16 of 18 targets for 204 yards and two touchdowns across Carolina's first two games this season, Coker has managed just 15 receptions on 35 targets for 189 yards and one touchdown over his last six contests. He remains second on the team in receptions (31), targets (53) and receiving yards (393) but likely can't be trusted after four consecutive performances of less than 10.0 fantasy points. However, Coker is in for a favorable Week 11 matchup against a Baltimore secondary that's allowed 9.2 yards per target to opposing wideouts through nine contests this year.

free_agents.name: Rachaad White
free_agents.outlook: Rachaad White is averaging at least four yards per carry over his last three games with the Commanders. Though White is technically the starting running back, he has only had double-digit carries twice this season. Moreover, Jacory Croskey-Merritt could return soon from Injured Reserve. For now, though, White remains the top dog in the backfield heading into a Week 11 clash with the Bengals. Cincy has been better against the pass than the run in 2026. The Bengals are allowing 123.9 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Chris Boswell
free_agents.outlook: In Week 11, Chris Boswell and the Steelers are back on the road to face the 2-7 Eagles. He connected on his only field goal attempt and lone PAT during Pittsburgh's 38-18 loss in Week 10. The Steelers offense struggled mightily to gain any traction until the game was well out of reach, leaving Boswell on the sidelines while his team opted to go for two on their final touchdown. He'll look to get more involved against a Philadelphia defense giving up 24.6 points per game this season.

free_agents.name: J.K. Dobbins
free_agents.outlook: J.K. Dobbins fell into a depth role behind rookie Jonah Coleman in the Broncos' backfield prior to the team's bye. Over the last three games, Dobbins has 17 carries to Coleman's 37, and the youngster is also seeing the bulk of the action at the goal line. Dobbins scored a rushing TD during that span, and he hasn't completely disappeared from the game plan, but it would likely take an injury to Coleman for him to log significant volume again. Dobbins will take on a Raiders defense in Week 11 that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Tyler Shough
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Shough is set to lead the Saints' offense into the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Shough had an underwhelming outing in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers, completing 25 of 35 pass attempts for 187 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Despite this, he remains tied for the second-most pass attempts per game (38.1) in the NFL this season, suggesting he'll have loads of opportunities for points as the year progresses. Shough is set to face a Bears defense that's given up just 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

free_agents.name: Tank Dell
free_agents.outlook: Tank Dell had just 21 yards on four targets in the Week 10 loss to Cleveland after turning nine targets into 105 yards and a TD in Houston's Week 9 win over the Chargers. The speedy wideout continues to offer big-play potential in Week 11 against the Colts, who give up 15.4 yards per catch to wide receivers. Dell's floor is low in Houston's deep WR room, but his ceiling is certainly high enough to warrant flex consideration, especially with surging QB C.J. Stroud having thrown 13 touchdown passes in the Texans' last four games.

free_agents.name: Kenny Gainwell
free_agents.outlook: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Despite Gainwell playing behind Bucky Irving, he's tallied 304 yards from scrimmage over the Buccaneers' last three games. Additionally, head coach Todd Bowles told reporters Monday that the team will aim to lessen Irving's workload going forward, suggesting Gainwell's role on the offense could expand as the year progresses. However, Gainwell may struggle against the Lions in Week 11, as the Detroit has allowed just 3.7 yards per carry to opposing running backs this year.

free_agents.name: Tyler Allgeier
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Allgeier and the Cardinals will face a tough Kansas City defense in Week 11. Allgeier struggled in this past Sunday's loss to the Rams, gaining only 14 yards on five carries and failing to catch his only target. What's more, he logged just a 44 percent offensive snap share despite the absence of Jeremiyah Love (ankle), who's slated to miss several more weeks. Allgeier may be splitting backfield work with Bam Knight against a sturdy KC run defense that is yielding the second-fewest yards per carry (3.46) to running backs this season.

free_agents.name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Marvin Harrison sat out Houston's Week 10 loss to the Browns due to a hamstring injury and is out again for Week 11 against the Colts. He won't be a trustworthy fantasy option for the foreseeable future while battling for targets in a deep Texans WR room that also includes Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte. Harrison has 11 catches for 145 yards and two touchdowns in seven games split between the Cardinals and Texans this season.

free_agents.name: Adonai Mitchell
free_agents.outlook: Adonai Mitchell continues to bring inefficiency through steady opportunity with the Jets set to face the Chargers in Week 11. Mitchell has 24 targets over the last three weeks but has converted them into just 10 catches, tallying a solid 201 yards. The Chargers' secondary is allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to wideouts, and Mitchell figures to see consistent volume, particularly with Omar Cooper (ankle) uncertain to play. But Geno Smith's ankle injury also brings ambiguity to this passing game, making Mitchell a high-upside, low-floor option.

free_agents.name: Xavier Hutchinson
free_agents.outlook: Xavier Hutchinson has scored in three consecutive games heading into Houston's Week 11 home game against the Colts. He's averaging six targets per game, and while his paltry average of 6.4 yards per target suggests C.J. Stroud would be better off distributing those looks elsewhere, Hutchinson's volume has propelled the 26-year-old wideout into the weekly flex conversation. Perhaps Hutchinson is just a late bloomer who is finding his groove, but it's fair to remain skeptical considering his three TDs in the last three games match his total of three TDs from 55 regular-season appearances before this streak. The Colts have limited WRs to eight TDs in 10 games, though Indianapolis is allowing 149 yards per game to the position.

free_agents.name: Makai Lemon
free_agents.outlook: Makai Lemon has been the top target for the Eagles of late due to several injuries, though that could change following the bye. Lemon has at least eight targets in three-straight contests, but DeVonta Smith and/or Dontayvion Wicks could return from the shelf in Week 11 versus the Steelers. While Lemon should still remain involved, his opportunities could decrease despite the favorable matchup with the Steelers. Pittsburgh is allowing 242.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Ryan Flournoy
free_agents.outlook: Ryan Flournoy has scored in three of the last five contests for the Cowboys. Flournoy has caught at least two passes in every game this season, and has drawn at least four targets in all but one contest. In Week 11, Flournoy has a tasty matchup against the Titans. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Pat Freiermuth
free_agents.outlook: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers visit the Eagles for an in-state showdown in Week 11. He caught two of three targets for 35 yards and one touchdown during Pittsburgh's Week 10 loss, making it two straight outings with a score. Freiermuth fought hard to break the goal line on his 27-yard TD reception, even with his team down big in the fourth quarter. He played 53% of the offensive snaps compared to 50% for Darnell Washington, so snap counts have essentially been a coin flip between the two tight ends. Freiermuth is a tough sell for fantasy managers in a matchup versus Philadelphia's defense, as they're tied for the fourth-fewest points allowed per game (10.5) to opposing TEs.

free_agents.name: Wan'Dale Robinson
free_agents.outlook: Wan'Dale Robinson hurt his ankle in Tennessee's Week 10 loss to the Jaguars. It remains to be seen if one, both, or neither of Robinson or Carnell Tate (shoulder) will be available to face the Cowboys in Week 11. Whichever wideouts earn the majority of playing time for the Titans in Week 11 could thrive against a Dallas secondary that's giving up 158 yards and a receiving touchdown per game to WRs. Robinson leads the Titans with 38 catches and three receiving TDs, but he's third on the team with 272 receiving yards through nine games, trailing Tate (413) and Elic Ayomanor (290). If Robinson plays, he's worth deploying as a flex option.

free_agents.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Omar Cooper is questionable to suit up for the Jets against the Chargers in Week 11 due to an ankle injury. Cooper managed just one snap in Week 10 as the same ankle that cost him four weeks earlier in the season flared up, resulting in his second game in three weeks without a catch. Pairing that with quarterback uncertainty, with Geno Smith also dealing with an ankle injury, Cooper profiles as a volatile, deep option against a secondary that's allowing the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing receivers.

free_agents.name: Kaelon Black
free_agents.outlook: Kaelon Black could be a key factor for San Francisco in Week 11 versus a tough Minnesota defense. The rookie running back has shown plenty of promise, and he's coming off a performance against the Cowboys during which he accounted for 66 total yards and a touchdown. Despite continuing to work behind superstar Christian McCaffrey, Black has recorded double-digit carries and at least 53 rushing yards in each of his past three games and has scored two touchdowns during that span. He's averaging a healthy 4.5 yards per carry on the season, which could give him plenty of importance against a Minnesota defense that is yielding an NFL-best 14.0 points per game but that ranks in the bottom half of the league with 4.26 yards per carry allowed to running backs.

free_agents.name: Caleb Douglas
free_agents.outlook: Caleb Douglas continues to make big plays on increased chances ahead of the the Dolphins' Week 11 game against the Bills. Douglas notched eight targets for the second-straight game in Week 10, reaching 70 yards for the third time in four outings. While new quarterback Kyle McCord threw 32 passes to 11 different teammates in his debut, Douglas remained the steady top option. Buffalo allows just 7.3 yards per target, the eighth-lowest in the league, but with Miami likely to be throwing from behind often, Douglas can be a preferred option.

free_agents.name: Juwan Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers in the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Johnson has really struggled over New Orleans' last four games, catching just five of 10 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown. With Jordyn Tyson breaking out in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers (11-80-0), Johnson will likely receive even less opportunities going forward. He likely needs to score a touchdown to find fantasy relevance in Week 11 against a Bears defense that's allowed just three touchdowns to tight ends all season.

free_agents.name: Matt Gay
free_agents.outlook: Matt Gay didn't get much volume in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, as he converted both his field goal attempts and his only PAT. The veteran kicker has handled two or fewer FG attempts in four of the last six games, but with rookie Fernando Mendoza replacing Kirk Cousins under center, the offense's efficiency could take a step backward and give Gay more field goal chances. He may not be much busier in Week 11 against a Broncos team allowing 20.7 points per game, ninth in the league.

free_agents.name: Dalton Schultz
free_agents.outlook: Dalton Schultz is coming off a bittersweet Week 10 performance against the Browns. He scored his first touchdown of the season on his only catch but was held to a single reception for the first time all season. The reliable TE is a borderline fantasy starter for Week 11 against the Colts; however, there are certainly higher-upside options to be found at the position. Schultz hasn't topped 45 yards since his 140-yard Week 2 outburst, which occurred while the Texans were without top WR Nico Collins, who has since recovered from a hamstring injury. The Colts have allowed seven TDs in 10 games to TEs, which is tied for fifth-most in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Brian Thomas Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Brian Thomas tied his season high with three catches in Week 10 against the Titans, but he produced just 29 yards and remains an afterthought in Jacksonville's prolific passing game. The 2024 first-round pick has just 13 receptions in nine games during what has been a disappointing third NFL season. With Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers both healthy and clearly ahead of him on the WR depth chart, Thomas has minimal fantasy appeal for a Week 11 matchup against a stingy Giants secondary. Even if one of Washington or Meyers were to get hurt, it's unclear if Thomas would inherit additional opportunities over Josh Cameron or Travis Hunter, so Thomas is safely droppable in all but the deepest formats.

free_agents.name: Malik Washington
free_agents.outlook: Malik Washington's opportunities continue to decline as the Dolphins get set to face the Bills in Week 11. Washington recorded three targets in Week 10, the third time in four weeks since Miami's Week 6 bye that he's failed to garner more looks. While Miami figures to throw from behind against Buffalo, Kyle McCord spread his 32 pass attempts in Week 10 across 11 different options, all while rookie Chris Bell was sidelined. With just one touchdown catch all season, Washington doesn't seem likely to pop against a defense that's allowed 11 touchdown catches to wide receivers, the fourth-highest total in the league.

free_agents.name: Mike Gesicki
free_agents.outlook: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Washington for a Week 11 tilt on Monday Night Football. He caught one of two targets for nine yards during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory, unable to capitalize on Joe Burrow throwing for 409 yards and four TDs. Gesicki now sports a 3-20-0 receiving line on four targets over his last two outings after catching a touchdown in each of his five previous games. He does, however, get a favorable matchup versus a Commanders defense allowing 20.2 fantasy points per game (31st) to opposing TEs.

free_agents.name: Kyler Murray
free_agents.outlook: Kyler Murray will look to get healthy in Week 11 as the Vikings play San Francisco. Murray hasn't seen the field since a Week 8 loss to Detroit, and the Vikings' trade for Kirk Cousins has essentially erased his value at this point in the season. If healthy, he'll aim to take away the current backup role from veteran Carson Wentz.

free_agents.name: Justice Hill
free_agents.outlook: Justice Hill and the Ravens are back on the road for an interconference clash against the Panthers in Week 11. He had three carries for four yards and caught five of seven targets for 34 yards during Baltimore's Week 10 defeat. Hill set new season highs in receptions and yardage with Jacoby Brissett making his team debut, a trend that could continue. Hill will try to exploit a Carolina defense allowing 27.3 fantasy points per game (29th) to opposing RBs.

free_agents.name: J.J. McCarthy
free_agents.outlook: J.J. McCarthy has thrown for at least 240 yards in three of the last four games for the Giants. McCarthy completed 23-of-36 passes for 293 yards, one touchdown and one interception last game versus the Commanders. The interception also came on a last-minute heave as the Giants attempted a comeback. In Week 11, the Giants will face a Jacksonville defense that has been mediocre against the pass in 2026. The Jags are allowing 228.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 19th in the NFL. However, Jacksonville has surrendered just 10 passing scores this season, which is fourth in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Evan McPherson
free_agents.outlook: In Week 11, Evan McPherson and the high-flying Bengals offense will travel to Washington for an interconference showdown. He went 1-for-2 on field goals while connecting on all five PATs during Cincinnati's 38-18 win in Week 10. McPherson's miss was his first of the season, so he'll be looking to get back on track versus a Commanders team allowing 24.8 points per game.

free_agents.name: Jason Sanders
free_agents.outlook: Jason Sanders surged into fantasy relevance for an inefficient Jets offense ahead of a Week 11 matchup with the Chargers. The Jets have been kept out of the end zone in consecutive games, forcing Sanders to kick four field goals in each outing, something he's now done in four of their last five games. Sanders has double-digit scoring potential against a defense that's allowing the fourth-most fantasy points per game to opposing kickers.

free_agents.name: Travis Hunter
free_agents.outlook: Travis Hunter generated 59 of his 91 receiving yards and his only touchdown of the campaign in Week 6 against the Texans. The 2025 second overall pick has the talent to produce a big play or two in any given game despite his limited usage on offense, but he has focused primarily on playing cornerback throughout his second NFL season. With Jacksonville's receiving corps healthy for Week 11 against the Giants, expect Hunter to remain off the fantasy radar, playing just a handful of snaps on offense.

free_agents.name: Fernando Mendoza
free_agents.outlook: Fernando Mendoza did the best he could in his first NFL start against an extremely tough opponent, as the Raiders lost to the Seahawks in Week 10. The rookie quarterback completed under 60% of his passes and didn't throw for a touchdown, but he also avoided committing a turnover and ran in a 10-yard score for Las Vegas' only TD. Mendoza could face another obstacle, as star tight end Brock Bowers suffered an ankle injury that might sideline him for a spell and leave the offense without any game-plan targets. Mendoza will do his best with what he has to work with in Week 11 against a Broncos defense that's tied for 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

free_agents.name: Quentin Johnston
free_agents.outlook: Quentin Johnston was nearly invisible in the Chargers' Week 10 win over the Ravens, catching his only target for six yards. Ladd McConkey missed the contest with a back issue, and in his absence, Tre' Harris stepped up as Justin Herbert's top downfield option. Johnston has just a single reception in four of his last five games, and his skill set seems to be a particularly poor fit for Mike McDaniel's quick-strike passing attack. He's unlikely to contribute much in Week 11 against a Jets secondary that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Audric Estime
free_agents.outlook: Audric Estime is expected to remain New Orleans' top short-yardage back in the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Estime was inefficient in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers, rushing seven times for six yards. It's a positive sign for Estime's fantasy outlook going forward that he still had a valuable role in New Orleans' offense, despite the return of lead-back Travis Etienne. However, Estime will likely have minimal fantasy value without finding the end zone. He's set to face a solid Bears defense that's given up just five rushing touchdowns to RBs this year.

free_agents.name: Elic Ayomanor
free_agents.outlook: Elic Ayomanor led the Titans with 79 receiving yards on 10 targets in the Week 10 loss against the Jaguars, as Carnell Tate (shoulder) didn't play and Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) exited early. If one or both of Tate and Robinson remain unavailable in Week 11, Ayomanor could make the most of another expanded role against a Dallas defense that's giving up 158 yards per game to WRs and has allowed 10 receiving TDs to the position in as many games. If you're considering Ayomanor for a flex spot in Week 11, keep in mind that he averaged just 25 receiving yards per game when Tate and Robinson were both playing, so Ayomanor's Week 11 fantasy viability will be tied to the availability of those two teammates.

free_agents.name: Chad Ryland
free_agents.outlook: Chad Ryland and a sputtering Arizona offense will face off against Kansas City in Week 11. Ryland accounted for all of Arizona's scoring this past Sunday in a loss to the Rams with a pair of field goals. The Cardinals managed just 123 total yards in the contest, which was rookie quarterback Carson Beck's NFL debut. Arizona doesn't figure to pour on the points against a KC defense that is allowing the third-fewest points (17.3) in the league, so Ryland could see limited opportunities again Sunday.

free_agents.name: Seth McGowan
free_agents.outlook: Seth McGowan set career highs with 12 carries and 77 rushing yards in the Colts' Week 10 win over the Dolphins while scoring a touchdown for the second consecutive game. Indianapolis has deployed McGowan as the 1B option behind Jonathan Taylor over the past couple of weeks, and the rookie seventh-round pick is quietly averaging an impressive 5.2 yards per carry in his young career. McGowan has yet to catch multiple passes in a game and has just nine career receiving yards, so he'll be tough to trust as a flex option, even in deeper formats, until he shows more receiving capabilities. He'll face a Texans defense in Week 11 that has been much more vulnerable through the air than on the ground, limiting RBs to 89 rushing yards per game.

free_agents.name: Tyjae Spears
free_agents.outlook: Tyjae Spears turned five touches into 28 yards in the Titans' Week 10 loss to Jacksonville in his first action since Week 6. The change-of-pace RB has dealt with ankle and knee injuries this season. The surging Tony Pollard is locked in as the top option in Tennessee's backfield, but Spears may be able to do enough with his handful of touches to warrant deep-league flex consideration for Week 11 against the Cowboys, who have been the most generous defense in the league to RBs. Dallas has allowed 16 TDs to the position through 10 games, as well as 155 scrimmage yards per game.

free_agents.name: Baker Mayfield
free_agents.outlook: Baker Mayfield (foot/ankle) is expected to lead the Buccaneers' offense if active for the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Mayfield sustained an injury to his foot and ankle area during the Week 9 loss to the Bears, putting his availability for Sunday's contest in jeopardy. Since returning from a thumb injury in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, Mayfield has completed 25 of 46 pass attempts for 307 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, suggesting his fantasy outlook is bleak going forward. However, he could find success against a Lions defense that's struggled this season, allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks (25.0) in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Mike Washington Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Mike Washington may be letting an opportunity to claim the early-down role in the Raiders' backfield slip through his fingers. Over the last two games, including a Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, the rookie running back has gained just 20 rushing yards on 14 carries. Ashton Jeanty hasn't been any better, but his receiving skills will keep him atop the depth chart for now. Washington will try to get rolling again in Week 11 against a Broncos defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Chris Rodriguez remains a touchdown dependent deep league flex option for Week 11, though his chances of cashing in aren't great against a Giants defense that has allowed just four rushing TDs to RBs all season. Rodriguez had a season low five yards in Jacksonville's Week 10 win over the Titans. He has scored on the ground in four of Jacksonville's nine games while rushing for at least 55 yards twice, but Rodriguez remains a non-factor as a receiver, with just four catches for 36 yards all season. Bhayshul Tuten remains the clear No. 1 RB for the Jaguars.

free_agents.name: Keon Coleman
free_agents.outlook: Keon Coleman isn't factoring heavily in the Bills' passing game entering a Week 11 matchup with the Dolphins. He was held to just one catch on three targets in Week 10, the fifth time in nine games he's secured just one reception, creating a low floor for the team's third receiving option. While Miami allows a generous 9.3 yards per target, they've surrendered only six touchdowns to wide receivers. Buffalo remains a run-heavy offense and likely won't need to throw often in Week 11 to beat an overmatched opponent, further limiting Coleman's chances.

free_agents.name: Geno Smith
free_agents.outlook: Geno Smith will need to overcome an ankle injury if he's to help the Jets take down the Chargers in Week 11. Smith was in and out of the lineup in Week 10, his first time ceding snaps under center all season, resulting in his second straight game without a touchdown pass. Smith now has one or zero scores in seven of his 10 outings. While the Chargers have allowed at least 340 passing yards in consecutive games, they've also surrendered multiple touchdown passes just three times in nine games, not setting Smith up for high-end production in Week 11. Cade Klubnik will start if Smith isn't deemed fit.

free_agents.name: Wil Lutz
free_agents.outlook: Wil Lutz comes out of the Broncos' Week 10 bye having converted multiple field goal attempts in three straight games and multiple PATs in five straight. The veteran kicker had a slow start to the season and still sits outside the top 20 in kicker scoring, but his recent consistency gives him a relatively stable floor, and playing his home games at altitude offers some upside. Lutz could be busy in Week 11 against a Raiders team that's allowed the most points per game in the league at 28.9, tied for 31st with the Cardinals.

free_agents.name: Jacoby Brissett
free_agents.outlook: In Week 11, Jacoby Brissett and the Ravens travel to face the Panthers in an interconference matchup. He completed 33 of 49 pass attempts for 340 yards with no TDs and one INT while rushing twice for two yards during his Baltimore debut in Week 10. Brissett connected with seven different receivers and led the Ravens to a final score above 13 points for the first time since Week 5. However, the team did lose its fifth game in a row, so Brissett will look to get into the win column versus a Carolina defense allowing 19.9 fantasy points per game (10th) to opposing QBs.

free_agents.name: Emari Demercado
free_agents.outlook: Emari Demercado could play a significant role for the Texans in Week 11 against the Colts. Woody Marks (concussion) won't play, while David Montgomery is suting up Thursday for his first action since Week 5. Demercado's appeal is limited to deep-league flex status in a change-of-pace role, though Montgomery may not be ready to take on a full workload against a Colts defense that's surrendering 151 scrimmage yards and a touchdown per game to RBs. Demercado averaged 6.5 yards per carry on 126 attempts spread across three years with the Cardinals, but that figure has plummeted to 2.6 yards per carry on 18 carries split between Dallas and Houston this season.

free_agents.name: Isiah Pacheco
free_agents.outlook: Isiah Pacheco will be out again in Week 11 as the Lions play the Buccaneers. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return this season in jeopardy. He's expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will continue to handle RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.

free_agents.name: Dontayvion Wicks
free_agents.outlook: Dontayvion Wicks could return from an ankle issue for the Eagles following their bye. Wicks has missed three-straight games for Philadelphia due to the ailment. His return, along with that of DeVonta Smith, would bolster an extremely depleted wide receiving corps. If he can suit up, the matchup could also be favorable in Week 11, as the Steelers defense has been surprisingly vulnerable to the pass in 2026. Pittsburgh is allowing 242.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Pat Bryant
free_agents.outlook: Pat Bryant returned from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury in the Broncos' final game before their Week 10 bye, catching four of five targets for 56 yards and a touchdown. It was his most productive outing of the season, but it also came as Jaylen Waddle left the contest early with a concussion. Bryant has shown some chemistry with Bo Nix, but assuming Waddle doesn't miss additional time, his target volume figures to remain limited. Bryant will try to return to the end zone in Week 11 against a Raiders secondary that ranks 24th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Daniel Jones
free_agents.outlook: Daniel Jones remains without a multi-TD performance this season, and he has minimal talent to work with after Indianapolis' trade-deadline selloff. One of his three wins in 10 tries came in Week 3 against the Texans, when Jones threw for 235 yards, one touchdown, and one interception against a Houston secondary that's allowing the sixth-most passing yards per game this season. Even repeating that stat line will be a challenge for Jones in the Week 11 rematch on the road, considering he's averaging just 183 passing yards per game and no remaining pass catcher on the Colts has more than 276 receiving yards. Jones is a bottom-five fantasy QB, making him an unappealing option even in superflex formats.

free_agents.name: Kimani Vidal
free_agents.outlook: Kimani Vidal nearly disappeared from the Chargers' game plan in their first win of the season. During a Week 10 win over the Ravens, he gained zero yards on two carries while catching both his targets for 14 yards, his lowest touch volume since Week 3. Omarion Hampton, meanwhile, broke out for 105 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries, potentially ending the team's backfield committee. Vidal will try to make a splash in Week 11 against a Jets defense that's tied for 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Malachi Fields
free_agents.outlook: Malachi Fields has caught at least two passes in every game during his rookie campaign for the Giants. In fact, he caught three passes for 62 yards last game, and has at least four targets in four-straight tilts. In Week 11, the Giants will face a Jacksonville defense that has been mediocre against the pass in 2026. The Jags are allowing 228.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 19th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Keaton Mitchell
free_agents.outlook: Keaton Mitchell nearly disappeared from the Chargers' game plan in their first win of the season. During a Week 10 victory over the Ravens, he failed to catch his only target and eked out just four rushing yards on three carries, after handling 17 total touches in the prior two contests. Omarion Hampton, meanwhile, broke out for 105 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries, potentially ending the team's backfield committee in decisive fashion. Mitchell will try to make a splash on what touches he gets in Week 11 against a Jets defense that's tied for 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Treylon Burks
free_agents.outlook: Treylon Burks returned from a foot injury following a one-game absence for Washington. He managed two catches for 27 yards in the 24-21 win over the Giants. Burks had three targets for the game. However, in Week 11, he will be facing a Bengals defense allowing just 216.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. In addition, Cincy has yielded only 11 passing scores, which is tied for fifth in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
free_agents.outlook: In Week 11, Ja'Kobi Lane and the Ravens are on the road for an interconference clash with the Panthers. He hauled in three of 11 targets for 61 yards during Baltimore's Week 10 loss. The rookie third-rounder set new career highs in yardage and targets, finishing third on the team in yardage and first in targets. Jacoby Brissett attempted 49 passes and threw for 340 yards in his team debut, and if the Ravens continue to throw at that rate, Lane could certainly develop into an intriguing fantasy prospect. However, managers need the rookie to convert his looks into real production, and his usage is an encouraging sign that should be monitored going forward.

free_agents.name: Bam Knight
free_agents.outlook: Bam Knight appears set to work in a backfield timeshare with Tyler Allgeier for the Cardinals in Week 11 against Kansas City. Knight returned from a one-game absence to face the Rams this past Sunday, and he logged a 56 percent offensive snap share to Allgeier's 44 percent. However, Knight didn't do much with the opportunity, gaining just 19 yards on five carries and going without a catch on two targets. Both running backs could find the sledding tough against a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in the NFL with 15.2 fantasy points per game allowed to running backs.

free_agents.name: Darnell Washington
free_agents.outlook: Darnell Washington and the Steelers travel to battle the Eagles for an interconference clash in Week 11. He corralled one of three targets for five yards during Pittsburgh's Week 10 loss, playing a season-low 50% of the offensive snaps. That can largely be attributed to the game being well out of hand for the Steelers, who trailed 31-3 going into the fourth quarter. Washington will aim to make more of an impact versus Philadelphia's stingy defense against TEs, as they're tied for the fourth-fewest fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to the position.

free_agents.name: Rashod Bateman
free_agents.outlook: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens visit the Panthers for a Week 11 interconference tilt. He caught three of five targets for 42 yards during Baltimore's Week 10 loss. The receptions, yardage and targets were the most for Bateman since he recorded a 5-62-0 line on six targets in Week 5. Jacoby Brissett attempted 49 passes and threw for 340 yards in his team debut, so there's at least some shred of possibility the Ravens can evolve into a more pass-friendly offense, but fantasy managers need Bateman to put up much bigger numbers before they consider starting him.

free_agents.name: Austin Ekeler
free_agents.outlook: Austin Ekeler has received at least eight touches in three-straight games for the Commanders. He rushed nine times for 26 yards in the most recent win over the Giants, while also catching four passes for 26 yards out of the backfield. However, Jacory Croskey-Merritt may return from injury in Week 11 versus the Bengals, which would reduce Ekeler's workload behind Rachaad White.  If Croskey-Merritt cannot suit up, Ekeler would see more opportunities against a Cincy defense surrendering 123.9 rushing yards per clash, which is 21st in the league.

free_agents.name: Ryan Fitzgerald
free_agents.outlook: Ryan Fitzgerald is expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Panthers' Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. Fitzgerald nailed a game-winning field goal as time expired during the Week 10 win over the Saints, making four of his five kicks. On the season, the second-year pro from Florida State has converted on 15 of 17 field-goal tries but just 18 of 23 point-after attempts. Fitzgerald figures to have loads of scoring chances in Week 11, as he faces a Ravens defense that's allowed 8.9 kicking points per game through nine contests this year.

free_agents.name: Kalif Raymond
free_agents.outlook: Kalif Raymond will remain a secondary option in the passing game in Week 11 as the Bears play the Saints. After an impressive start to the season, Raymond has petered out with just one game over 20 receiving yards since Week 3. The veteran will take a 32-290-1 receiving line into a tough matchup against a New Orleans defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

free_agents.name: Mason Taylor
free_agents.outlook: Mason Taylor brings low volume in an otherwise promising matchup in Week 11 when the Jets face the Chargers. Taylor hasn't collected more than six targets all season while topping 33 yards just once, but with Omar Cooper (ankle) potentially sidelined, more targets could be available in Week 11. The Chargers have allowed only one touchdown to tight ends but have surrendered over 100 yards to the position twice in the last four weeks, giving Mason potential for a yardage uptick.

free_agents.name: Darius Cooper
free_agents.outlook: Darius Cooper had a season-high eight targets last game for the Eagles. Unfortunately, he managed just two catches for 25 yards despite the extra looks. DeVonta Smith and/or Dontayvion Wicks could return from  injury following the bye, which would shift Cooper back down the depth chart despite the favorable Week 11 matchup with the Steelers. Pittsburgh is allowing 242.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Cade Otton
free_agents.outlook: Cade Otton is expected to remain one of Tampa Bay's top receiving options during the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Otton received a season-high eight targets in the Week 9 loss to the Bears, logging four receptions for 25 yards. On the season, he ranks third on the Buccaneers in targets (38) and receptions (23) while ranking fourth in receiving yards (211). Otton could really thrive in Week 11, as Detroit's defense has allowed a whopping 22.9 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season, the most in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Tre' Harris
free_agents.outlook: Tre' Harris was the Chargers' top pass catcher in their first win of the season, a Week 10 victory over the Ravens. With Ladd McConkey sidelined by a back issue, Harris stepped up and caught all five of his targets for a season-high 86 yards. The second-year wide receiver is still looking for his first touchdown of the season, but with the Chargers' offense showing flickers of life, Harris appears to have surpassed Quentin Johnston in the pecking order for looks from Justin Herbert. McConkey could be back in Week 11, however, which would make it more difficult for Harris to maintain his momentum against a Jets secondary that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Kayshon Boutte
free_agents.outlook: Kayshon Boutte crashed back down to earth with a zero-catch performance in Week 10 against the Browns. That season-worst outing followed a 125-yard, two-TD outburst in Week 9 against the Chargers. Boutte's likely to land somewhere in between those two extremes in Week 11 against the Colts, though the Week 10 goose egg is closer to what should be expected of the depth wideout. He's averaging just 24 receiving yards in the eight games excluding his effort against the Chargers, with no TDs as a member of the Texans outside of that outing, either.

free_agents.name: Joe Milton
free_agents.outlook: Joe Milton's first NFL start for the Eagles resulted in a loss, but there were promising signs. Milton did not throw an interception, and he also flashed his dual-threat ability with 64 yards versus the Giants. However, Milton completed only 52.9-percent of his throws for just 169 yards. He could get both DeVonta Smith as well as Dontayvion Wicks back from injury in Week 11 versus the Steelers, which would bolster an extremely depleted wide receiving corps. In addition, the Eagles will face a Steelers defense that has been surprisingly vulnerable to the pass in 2026. Pittsburgh is allowing 242.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Jake Elliott
free_agents.outlook: Jake Elliott has made just seven field goals on the entire season for the Eagles. Yes, you read that correctly. In nine contests, Elliott has only attempted eight field goals. The struggles of the Philadelphia offense have been well-documented this season, even before the Jalen Hurts injury saga. With third-string quarterback Joe Milton under center in Week 11 versus the Steelers, optimism is not high for a sudden uptick in scoring. Even following a poor defensive performance versus Cincinnati, the Steelers are still allowing just 20.2 points per tilt, which is seventh in the league.

free_agents.name: Roschon Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Roschon Johnson is likely to be a depth option as the Bears play New Orleans in Week 11. Johnson has mostly benefited from the absence of Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb), but he didn't play a snap on offense in a Week 9 win over Tampa Bay, even with Monangai remaining inactive. Monangai could also return in the upcoming home front, which would shrink Johnson's role even more. The Saints have ranked a favorable 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs, but Johnson's fluctuating role makes him a tough play.

free_agents.name: Jauan Jennings
free_agents.outlook: Jauan Jennings will seek to make a return as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. Jennings sat out in Week 10 with a calf injury, which was his second miss of the season. The veteran has now recorded six catches for 54 yards across six games. If he's able to play, he could see an uptick in usage with Jordan Addison (thumb) out. San Francisco has ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to WRs this campaign.

free_agents.name: Myles Price
free_agents.outlook: Myles Price could benefit from an uptick in usage again as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. With teammates Jordan Addison (thumb) and Jauan Jennings (calf) both out in Week 10, Price caught four targets for 49 yards and a touchdown and rushed the ball once for 12 yards, which were all season highs or tied season highs. With Addison set to be out for multiple weeks and Jennings not showing much when on the field, Price could be the flashy target opposite Justin Jefferson that Minnesota needs. Price look to keep his success going against a San Francisco defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to his position.

free_agents.name: Chimere Dike
free_agents.outlook: Chimere Dike had 71 receiving yards and a touchdown catch in Tennessee's Week 8 loss to the Bengals, but that performance accounts for more than half of his 140 receiving yards this season. Dike could be ticketed for a larger role in Week 11 against the Cowboys if at least one of Carnell Tate (shoulder) or Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) doesn't play. The 2025 fourth-round pick has stepped up when given more opportunities before, but Dike remains a deep-league dart throw at best in most formats, even against a weak Dallas secondary that's allowing 158 receiving yards per game to WRs, considering Tennessee's passing game has ranged from putrid to inconsistent. In fantasy formats that reward punt and kickoff return yards, you're probably starting him for his special-teams contributions regardless, with any offensive output just a nice bonus.

free_agents.name: Jalen Nailor
free_agents.outlook: Jalen Nailor's supporting role in the Raiders' offense didn't change in Week 10 as the team transitioned from Kirk Cousins to rookie Fernando Mendoza under center. In Mendoza's first NFL start, Nailor caught just one of four targets for a loss of one yard. The former Viking has handled at least four targets in five straight games, but he has just a 10-69-1 line on 21 targets to show for that volume. He'll try to build better chemistry with Mendoza in Week 11 against a Broncos secondary that ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Gunnar Helm
free_agents.outlook: Gunnar Helm has exceeded 28 receiving yards just once in the Titans' first nine games this season and has yet to score a TD. However, he has 12 catches in the last three games after recording just nine receptions through six games. The second-year TE is trending in the right direction ahead of a Week 11 matchup with a Dallas defense that ranks in the middle of the pack at defending the position, largely because opponents haven't had to involve their TEs as much while carving up the Cowboys' defense with RB and WR production. Helm will have to build more momentum to be considered for a fantasy starting role, but dynasty league managers should take note of the 2025 fourth-round pick's recent uptick.

free_agents.name: Drew Stevens
free_agents.outlook: Drew Stevens managed just one field goal last game for Washington. It was just the third time this season that the kicker for the Commanders failed to boot multiple field goals in a game. However, he did nail all three of his extra-points in the 24-21 win over the Giants. In Week 11, Stevens will face a Bengals squad allowing 21.4 points per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
